Subject: Redwood POC — proposed SOW and exit / ramp language

Hi Ellen,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — great walkthrough. Attached is the updated SOW (MedSys_SOW_v2.pdf) and a simple ramp table (ramp_schedule_table.xlsx) that lays out the committed throughput by month for the 6-month POC.

Per our conversation, we included two items we know procurement will watch closely: an early-exit (escape hatch) clause and a graduated ramp schedule. Quick summary:
- Escape hatch: Either party may terminate the POC within the first 60 days with a 30-day notice; if MedSys elects early termination we propose a one-time credit equal to 50% of the remaining committed monthly fees (applied as account credit).
- Graduated ramp: Month 1–2: 25% committed baseline, Month 3–4: 60%, Month 5–6: 100% (full commit). See attached spreadsheet for numbers.

I want to flag that the escape hatch is non-standard relative to our typical phased-commit deals; I'm noting it up-front so we can align quickly if procurement asks for adjustments. If you'd prefer a different construct (e.g., pro-rated refund instead of credit, or a 30-day opt-out window instead of 60) say the word and we can circulate alternatives.

Attachments: MedSys_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW w/ proposed language), ramp_schedule_table.xlsx

Next steps: Once you confirm procurement's preference on the opt-out mechanics I'll escalate internally for the small concession needed on the credit calculation.

Best,
David

Marissa / Vivek —

Looping you in for a quick deal-desk escalation. MedSys (high strategic value: major regional health system, potential $1.2M ARR if POC converts) is asking to change two SOW items from our draft:

Ask summary (MedSys requests):
- Opt-out: reduce escape hatch window from 60 days -> 30 days; require pro-rated refund of any pre-paid fees (instead of account credit).
- Ramp floor: maintain minimum committed floor of 40% for months 3–4 (our draft had 25% -> 60% sequence).

Why this is non-standard / risk:
- Financial exposure: pro-rated refunds increase near-term revenue churn risk vs. credits.
- Operational: shorter opt-out reduces our time to realize value; could increase churn if integration delays occur.
- Upside: closing this POC with MedSys creates a strong reference and opens multiple internal buying centers.

Proposed commercial compromise (what I recommend we approve if you sign off):
- Approve 30-day opt-out with pro-rated refund limited to pre-paid usage for the remaining calendar month only (cap = 50% of one month’s committed fee). This limits downside versus full pro-ration of the remainder of the term.
- Approve ramp floor 40% for months 3–4, but maintain requirement that month 5–6 reach 100% commit or contract converts to annual tiered pricing.
- No change to list price; concession is a limited early-termination refund cap (one-time) — expected revenue impact under worst reasonable-case: ~$18k (one-time).

Attachments: I attached the SOW and ramp table again for visibility. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/MSH-2027-0031

Request: Please advise approval (yes / yes with modification / no) ASAP — procurement is scheduling a legal review tomorrow.

Thanks,
David
